title: The five-hour rule for AI training | Traq Collective
h1: The five-hour rule for AI training
metaDescription: A single AI workshop rarely changes how a team works. Past roughly five hours of hands-on practice, people cross from one-time triers into regular users.
targetQuery: how much AI training does a team need
author: Nazir Dogan
dek: One workshop is not a programme. The habit forms after real practice, not a demo.
intro: The five-hour rule is a simple way to size AI training: below about five hours of hands-on practice, most people stay one-time triers, and above it they become regular users. A single lunch-and-learn almost never sticks. What changes behaviour is repeated practice on real tasks, spread over the first few weeks.

body.heading: Why one workshop does not change how a team works
paragraphs: It is tempting to book one AI workshop, tick the training box, and move on. The problem is that comfort with a new tool comes from reps, not from watching a demo. People need to try AI on their own work, get it wrong, adjust, and get a result they trust, more than once, before it becomes a habit they reach for without being told.

body.heading: How much practice a team actually needs
paragraphs: That is why we build training as a short programme rather than an event. A first hands-on session gets people a quick win, then follow-up practice on their real tasks pushes them past the point where the habit holds. Role-specific beats generic here: the marketing team and the finance team should practise on their own jobs, not a shared toy example.

body.heading: Treat five hours as a planning floor, not a target
paragraphs: The number is not magic, and it is not a certificate. It is a planning floor. If your team has had one hour of AI training, do not expect regular use yet. Budget for the practice, and the adoption follows.

takeaway: Plan for at least five hours of hands-on AI practice per person over the first month, on their real work, not one all-hands session.

stat.claim: People who get more than five hours of training become regular AI users at far higher rates than those who get less.

faqs.q: How many hours of AI training does a team actually need?
faqs.a: Treat roughly five hours of hands-on practice as a planning floor rather than a target. Below that, most people try AI once and drift back to old habits. The hours only count when people are working on their own real tasks, not watching a demo.

faqs.q: Is one AI workshop enough to change how a team works?
faqs.a: Rarely. A single session can get people a first win, but comfort with a new tool comes from repetition. Plan a short programme with follow-up practice on real work instead of a one-off event.
